verdict.line: You lose if you let Gnar poke you down with Boomerang Throw and never close distance before level 6; you win if you abuse Mega Gnar's transformation window with Parrrley poke and all-in before he hits max Rage.

brief.thesis: Gnar is strongest as mini-Gnar kiting with Boomerang Throw (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown) and weakest the instant he transforms, since Mega Gnar's W (Wallop) and E (Crunch) are short-range commitments with no escape. Gangplank's Q (Parrrley) outranges mini-Gnar's auto-attacks at level 1-2 and his poison passive (Grog-Soaked Blade) punishes every trade Gnar takes to build Rage, so the longer the lane goes the more the Rage bar works against the Gnar player, not for him.

theirWindow.when: mini-Gnar kiting with ranged Q poke
theirWindow.what: Don't walk up into Boomerang Throw range (1100) for free; farm with Parrrley from 625 range instead and let his boomerang cooldown (up to 16s at rank 1) sit idle while you poke back.

yourWindow.when: Rage bar nearly full or just after mini-Gnar E
yourWindow.what: He is about to transform or has just used Hop (22/19.5/17/14.5/12s cooldown) with no bounce target nearby — walk up and stack two or three Q's plus autos before Mega Gnar's stun threat (W Wallop) comes online.

boots.why: Highest winrate boots (52% over 891 games) — the flat physical damage reduction blunts his auto-attack and Boomerang Throw poke through the laning phase.

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks a DoT on top of your Grog-Soaked Blade poison on every Q poke, compounding damage against a kiting mini-Gnar who can't cleanse it

summoners.why: Run in 88.5% of games at 52% winrate — Ignite punishes his low early HP pool through Remove Scurvy's cleanse-and-heal, since it can't remove a DoT already ticking.

playing.title: Poke with Q, never autos
playing.detail: Use Parrrley (5s cooldown, 625 range) to farm and harass from outside Boomerang Throw's 1100 range threat zone whenever he's walked up to throw it.

playing.title: Save W for CC, not sustain
playing.detail: Remove Scurvy clears crowd control and heals, but its 22-18s cooldown means you should hold it specifically to cleanse Mega Gnar's R slow or wall-stun, not just to top off HP.

playing.title: All-in right after his E or Hop whiffs
playing.detail: If mini-Gnar's Hop (22-12s cooldown) has no minion or champion to bounce off, he's stuck in place — this is your window to walk up and land 2-3 Q's plus full autos.

playing.title: Respect the Rage bar at level 6+
playing.detail: Once his Rage is visibly near full, assume Mega Gnar is one ability away — don't commit to extended trades where his W (Wallop) stun or E (Crunch) AoE can land clean.

playing.title: Track his GNAR! cooldown after first use
playing.detail: R (GNAR!) is 90/60/30/0/0s cooldown by rank — once he's rank 3+, the ultimate is nearly always up, so don't facecheck brush or overextend near walls where the stun bonus damage triggers.

playing.title: Use E for lane pressure, not just allies
playing.detail: Raise Morale's AD and move speed buff (20s cooldown, 1200 range) helps you win short trades even without allies nearby — fire it before an all-in to close the gap faster.

playing.title: Bank R for sieges, not lane kills
playing.detail: Cannon Barrage's 120/115/110/120/120s cooldown is too slow to rely on in-lane; save it to zone him off waves or punish a Mega Gnar overextension near your tower.
